# News & Events
# Celebrating 100 Years of Excellence in Delden
10 Jun 2026
For a full century, the site along the Langestraat has been a familiar landmark for anyone passing through this corner of Twente. The chimney that once bore the name Servo is long gone, but the chemical company behind it, today known as KLK Kolb Specialties B.V., part of KLK OLEO Surfactants, remains deeply woven into the fabric of the region. A centenary worth celebrating.
The seven-hectare site is a world of its own. Laboratories, research facilities and towering reactors holding tens of thousands of litres operate virtually without pause, the only exception being public holidays. Visitors quickly learn the rules: beyond a clearly marked yellow line, only specially approved mobile phones are permitted. Safety is non-negotiable in this industry.
**From Delden into Every Home**
The plant does not manufacture finished consumer products. Instead, it produces surfactants, which are surface-active agents that allow oil and water to mix, or make substances soluble that would otherwise refuse to dissolve. These chemical building blocks end up in shampoos, laundry detergents, wall paints and textiles. In other words, there is a good chance something made in Delden is sitting in your home right now.
**From a Steam Laundry to a Global Group**
The story begins in 1926, when two local entrepreneurs, Kuiper and Rozenbroek, set up shop in a disused steam laundry after their original plan to build in Enschede fell through. They served the Twente textile industry, and during the Second World War even pivoted to food production when circumstances demanded it.
Decades of growth, restructuring and ownership changes followed. Locally the site is still affectionately called Servo, even though that name was officially retired in 2000 and the iconic chimney demolished in 2018. Today the company is owned by Swiss-based Kolb Distribution Ltd., itself part of KLK OLEO, the oleochemical arm of Malaysian conglomerate Kuala Lumpur Kepong Berhad.
**More Than Just a Factory**
The site is unusually well-equipped for an industrial location. It has its own volunteer fire brigade, a dedicated wastewater treatment plant, and most remarkably, a private railway spur that branches off the Zutphen–Oldenzaal line and runs directly onto the premises. Freight trains have used this connection for decades to deliver raw materials straight to the factory floor.
The railway has not always run without incident. In the early 1980s a wrongly set switch accidentally directed a passenger train onto the site. It was stopped in time, nobody was hurt, and the story has since become part of company folklore.
**Three Generations, Fifty-Year Careers**
Walk through the site with a long-serving colleague and you quickly sense that this is more than just a workplace. Over 200 people are employed here, the vast majority from Delden and the wider Twente area, with many of them cycling in each morning. Staff turnover is remarkably low: three employees recently marked 40 years of service, and last year one colleague reached 50. There are families where three generations have worked on the same site, and farmers’ sons who once looked for a temporary job and never left. That kind of loyalty speaks for itself.
**Centenary Celebrations**
The anniversary programme ran across several days. A business reception took place on Thursday 30 April, followed on Friday 1 May by a gathering for retirees and former staff, with dignitaries including the mayor, a provincial executive and the Count of Twickel in attendance, and an evening party for current employees.
On Saturday 2 May, the site opened its doors to the general public. As production continues around the clock and safety rules are strict, visitors were guided around the grounds by bus. The programme included live demonstrations by the company fire brigade and a kids’ science lab.
**From a small chemical supplier for the local textile industry to a global player in specialty chemistry; one hundred years of growth, resilience and community. The story of KLK Kolb Specialties is far from over, and the next hundred years have already begun.**
![KLK Kolb 100 Years Anniversary](https://www.klkoleo.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/KLK-Kolb-100-Years-Anniversary.png)

# News & Events
# Commander of the Order of Leopold II Award
30 Aug 2021
The King of Belgium has conferred upon the CEO of [Kuala Lumpur Kepong Berhad (“KLK”)](http://www.klk.com.my/) Tan Sri Dato’ Seri Lee Oi Hian the Commander of the Order of Leopold II during a private ceremony on 26 August 2021.
The prestigious National Order was officially presented to Tan Sri Lee on behalf of King Philippe of the Belgians by the Ambassador of Belgium to Malaysia His Excellency Pascal Grégoire. This award is given in honour of [KLK Tensachem’](https://tensachem.com/)s (part of KLK OLEO) transformation and contribution to the Sovereign of Belgium.

This Order, which was established on 24 August 1900, is awarded for meritorious service to the Sovereign of Belgium by Royal Decree, as a token of His personal goodwill. According to Mr Ambassador Grégoire, the Order is roughly equivalent to the British Victorian Order, which is a personal gift as well of the British monarch and has similar cases.
![](https://www.klkoleo.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/KLK-Tensachem.jpg)An ariel view of KLK Tensachem S.A. production site in Ougrée, Belgium
It was an honour to have other dignitaries to witness the momentous occasion. Also present at the ceremony was newly appointed Ambassador of Malaysia to Belgium H.E. Dato’ Ahmad Rozian Abd Ghani, Ambassador of the European Union to Malaysia H.E. Mr Michalis Rokas, Berjaya’s Tan Sri Dato’ Seri Vincent Tan and Belgium Embassy’s Deputy Head of Mission Mr Pierrick Massaux. The KLK OLEO team was represented by KLK OLEO CEO Mr Madhev Bala Subramaniam, Managing Director FAL & ME SBU Mr Raghunathan Nair and Managing Director MES Mr Chua Boon Hook.
![](https://www.klkoleo.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/Group1.jpg)Above from L-R: Ambassador of Malaysia to Belgium H.E. Dato’ Ahmad Rozian Abd Ghani, Tan Sri Lee Oi Hian, Tan Sri Vincent Tan, Belgium Ambassador H.E. Mr. Pascal Grégoire and Ambassador of the European Union to Malaysia H.E. Mr Michalis Rokas.

# News & Events
# KLK awarded Malaysia’s Best Managed Companies for third consecutive year
20 Sep 2024
![KLK Malaysia’s Best Managed Companies in 2024 Collage](https://www.klkoleo.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Collage.jpg)
KLK has once again been recognised as one of Malaysia’s Best Managed Companies in 2024. This marks the third consecutive year we have received this honour, reflecting our Company’s organisational success and contributions to the industry. The awards ceremony took place on 22 August, at Le Meridien Kuala Lumpur.
This year was particularly special, as KLK’s Executive Chairman, Tan Sri Lee Oi Hian was invited to be a guest speaker to share his insights on “Empowering the Next Generation for Business.”
Tan Sri Lee paid tribute to his father, the late Founder Chairman Tan Sri Lee Loy Seng, during his speech. He shared his experience as a second-generation leader and how he continued to build upon his father’s legacy. Additionally, he highlighted Tan Sri Lee Loy Seng’s subtle yet impactful mentorship and shared three valuable lessons:
  1. **Core** **Values** : “Integrity, humility, loyalty.” Values that Tan Sri Lee Loy Seng lived by, which continue to guide KLK’s dominant culture of **T**.**H**.**R**.**I**.**I**.**L**.
  2. **Purpose** **in** **life** : Finding fulfilment in life goes beyond wealth. It’s about creating a compassionate environment that impacts KLK’s 50,000 employees and their families. Tan Sri Lee Loy Seng reminded us to be good stewards of our stakeholders. Fulfilling this stewardship brings true contentment to life.
  3. **Balancing** **work** **and** **family** : His ability to manage the demands of running a business while fostering family unity and solidarity.

KLK’s COO, Mr. Lee Jia Zhang, accepted the award on behalf of KLK. Ms. Lee Wen Ling, Managing Director of KLK Land, was also invited onstage to answer a few questions about the win.
When asked about the perception of the plantation industry as being part of the “old economy,” Ms. Lee responded: “I believe this view is inaccurate. As consumers become more conscious, there is a growing demand for sustainably produced products. To stay ahead, we must continue exploring and adapting, going beyond sustainability certifications to focus on areas like decarbonisation and traceability, among others.”
Also present at the award gala dinner were KLK Head of Corporate Mr. Teh Kwan Wey and Sustainability & Special Projects AGM Mr. Adrian Tan.

[KL-Kepong Oleomas Sdn Bhd (“KLKOM”)](https://www.klkoleo.com/kl-kepong-oleomas-sdn-bhd/) has successfully added [Sodium Lauryl Sulphate (“SLS”)](https://www.klkoleo.com/our-product/tensopol-alcohol-sulphates/) and[ Sodium Lauryl Ether Sulphate (“SLES”)](https://www.klkoleo.com/our-product/tensagex-alcohol-ether-sulphates/) into their product portfolio since the first quarter (Q1) of 2021. KLKOM is the second SLS and SLES production site of KLK OLEO group after [KLK Tensachem, Belgium](https://tensachem.com/). The SLS and SLES manufactured by KLKOM are GMP-certified.
The addition of these two products makes the offering from KLK OLEO in Asia more complete, especially in the home and personal care industry.
###### [Sodium Lauryl Sulphate (TENSOPOL SLS)](https://www.klkoleo.com/our-product/tensopol-alcohol-sulphates/)
KLK OLEO produces [TENSOPOL SLS](https://www.klkoleo.com/our-product/tensopol-alcohol-sulphates/) with 100% renewable carbon. It is biodegradable, does not bio-accumulate in water or land, and has a natural origin index of 0.9 in accordance with ISO 16128. KLKOM can produce SLS in the form of needles, powder, as well as liquid.
SLS is one of the primary surfactants widely used in oral care, personal care and home care. SLS is also an effective surfactant used extensively in industrial applications to make floor cleaners, engine degreasers and machine wash detergents. Toothpaste can also use SLS in a lower concentration.
![](https://www.klkoleo.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/news-n-events-sls-sles-img01.jpg)
###### [Sodium Lauryl Ether Sulphate (TENSAGEX SLES)](https://www.klkoleo.com/our-product/tensagex-alcohol-ether-sulphates/)
SLES is an anionic surfactant, widely used as a primary surfactant in rinse-off products, such as dishwashing liquid and shampoo.
Produced from natural fatty alcohols, [TENSAGEX SLES](https://www.klkoleo.com/our-product/tensagex-alcohol-ether-sulphates/) features very high purity and low in 1,4-dioxane, salt and colour. It meets the latest regulatory restrictions for household cleaning products and personal care products.
[TENSAGEX SLES](https://www.klkoleo.com/our-product/tensagex-alcohol-ether-sulphates/) is available as a high-active paste and also in the form of low active liquid for easy processing.
![](https://www.klkoleo.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/news-n-events-sls-sles-img02.jpg)
With state-of-the-art technology to be completed at the end of 2021, SLES with 1 moles EO produced from KLKOM could achieve 1,4 dioxane specs at 5ppm max, which is one of the most stringent specs in the industry.

Since turning Pro as independent players, Peng Soon-Liu Ying have done well by winning the 2019 Thailand Masters and New Zealand Open.

An independent human rights risk assessment has been completed in our plantation operations in Peninsular Malaysia, with ongoing assessment in Sabah and Indonesia next in line.

In FY 2024, KLK for the first time obtained limited assurance on selected Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) and the Zoological Society of London’s Sustainable Palm Oil Transparency Toolkit (SPOTT) indicators.

This upgrade affirms KLK’s ongoing efforts to integrate sustainability into our business operations. This recognition is a testament to the dedication of all colleagues and it serves as a strong foundation for our continued journey towards sustainable growth and responsible stewardship.
